messages:
ara: Heads-up — noticed a ~7% p99 regression on long-seq workloads after yesterday's kernel-autotune rollout. Regression only shows up when KV cache hit > 0.

ara: quick profile snippet from prod (cold vs warm):
```
seq=1024, kv_hits=0 -> pick: fast-attn-v2 (latency 86ms)
seq=1024, kv_hits=12 -> pick: generic-fallback (latency 92ms)
stack: pick_decision -> arch_match -> kv_policy -> fallback_path
```

mike: ugh. so autotuner is preferring a more generic path when cache is warm. Flaky heuristics maybe penalize assumed memory locality? :thinking:

jin: can you paste the pick_reason metadata? we should have telemetry for this if REDWOOD_PICK_TRACE was enabled.

ara: i dug into traces — reasons field is "arch_mismatch OR estimated_scratch_exceeded" for the kv_hits case. Estimated scratch looks higher because KV inflates working set in our model of peak activation.

mike: that matches suspicion. autotuner's cost model doesn't account for distributed KV cache extents. It treats kv presence as extra per-request memory, so kernel selector chooses safer generic kernel.

jin: we can temporarily flip KERNEL_DEBUG_MODE=picktrace to force capture of decision context for a sample of requests and then run the offline estimator with kv-aware memory shape. command to enable on a dedicated canary:
```sh
export REDWOOD_PICK_TRACE=1
export KERNEL_DEBUG_MODE=picktrace
./infra/run_canary --route seqlen-1024 --sample-rate 0.02
```

ara: did that for one canary, attached trace snippet (non-sensitive):
```
{"chosen":"generic-fallback","reasons":["estimated_scratch_exceeded","quant_hint_mismatch"],"estimated_scratch":1.24e9,"hw":"A100-80GB"}
```

mike: 1.24GB scratch seems... high but plausible with our current kv accounting. Could be a telemetry bug: we may be double-counting k-vcache pages when kv_hits>0.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered canary: canary-id=ci-2026-13 seqlen-route sample-rate=0.02

jin: quick workaround for critical path: override kernel selection for seqlen>=512 when hw in [A100-80GB,NVIDIA-H] and kv_hits<=N to force fast-attn-v2. We can push a config override: K_PICK_OVERRIDES='{ "cond": "seqlen>=512 && hw =~ /A100/ && kv_hits < 32", "force":"fast-attn-v2" }'

ara: i pushed a conservative override to the canary config and saw p99 drop back to baseline in that canary (local sample). But we should be careful — could cause OOM on some extreme tails.

mike: action items: 1) add kv-aware scratch accounting to autotuner estimator (jin), 2) add an integration test that simulates kv_hits distribution and measures kernel choice (ara), 3) add picktrace sampling for 24h across prod regions (ops) and collect traces for analysis.

jin: i'll own the estimator change. plan: adjust memory model to include per-kv-entry live bytes and a separate cap for scratch usage derived from live activations minus kv_cache_saved. will submit PR with bench results.

ara: created a short repro harness in eng-runtime: repo/bench/kv-seqlen-sim. will add unit to CI.

deploy-bot: rollout halted to 2% pending canary validation (reason: kernel selection regression suspected)

mike: good call. let's keep the override in canary for 48h and then evaluate traces. Also, add a telemetry metric "pick_reason:estimated_scratch_exceeded" to alerted dashboards so we can graph correlation with kv hit rates.

ara: noted. i'll add dashboard panel and an alert with 1-hour aggregation if the metric spikes >0.5% of traffic.

jin: for visibility — i'm going to add a debug env flag that writes the estimator inputs to s3 for failing cases: REDWOOD_PICK_DUMP=1. only for sample-rate 0.001 so we don't blow up logs.

ara: thanks. leaves: I'll collect canary traces and post a short summary in an hour. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks team. keeping this thread as ground truth for followups.
